text: Tonight, two of Meridian Finworks' automation credentials go bad at once: an Azure service principal used by the nightly reporting job, and an AWS IAM access key used by a data-sync job. This lab runs the full detection, containment, and remediation sequence for both, under the same time pressure a real on-call engineer would feel.

The Azure Activity Log shows the sign-in coming from an unfamiliar ASN, followed by quiet Microsoft Graph enumeration calls listing directory roles and applications. Then comes the event that matters most: addPassword, added to the service principal's own application registration. That's the persistence step from Lesson 25 -- a second credential the attacker controls, independent of whatever secret actually leaked first.

Containment doesn't wait for the investigation to finish. Setting accountEnabled to false blocks every credential on that application at once, old and new. Every client secret gets deleted, a fresh one gets issued and stored in Key Vault, and the service principal's Graph permissions get cut down to exactly the read-only finance scope the reporting job actually needs.

On the AWS side, CloudTrail shows the identical shape of attack: quiet GetCallerIdentity and ListBuckets calls, then CreateAccessKey on the same IAM user -- persistence again, this time AWS's version of addPassword -- followed by a PutObject call against a bucket this sync job was never meant to touch.

Both of meridian-sync-user's access keys get deactivated immediately, not deleted, which blocks them from being used while preserving them as evidence. A deny-all policy goes on as a second layer in case a session token is still valid. Once the investigation closes, both old keys get deleted and one new, narrowly scoped key takes their place.

In both clouds, rotating only the originally leaked secret would have left the attacker's own added credential standing. Lesson 31 moves from a credential compromise to a different kind of incident entirely: a single over-broad RBAC role that exposed far more of Meridian's subscription than anyone intended.
